story: The Office of the Texas Governor directed the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality on September 21st, 2026 to issue no permits sought by data centers until ERCOT completes the interconnection audit ordered on August 3rd. The halt is written on two scopes at once. One sentence is about WHO is asking, and one is about the interconnection queue, and a project that never enters that queue produces no audit information to align a permitting decision to.

claims.quote: Governor Greg Abbott directed the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (TCEQ) to suspend action on all permits sought by data center projects until the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) completes its ongoing audit
claims.source_title: Troutman Pepper Locke, Governor Abbott Directs TCEQ to Halt All Data Center Permits Pending ERCOT/TWDB Audits

rejected.finding: Crusoe's gas plant air permit 182126 at the Abilene data center campus in Taylor County, with its comment window and the route to comment.
rejected.reason: NOTHING ABOUT IT IS VERIFIED and the whole finding is dropped. The notice PDF serves HTTP 200 and its text streams do not extract. A first read of it returned an applicant name, a reference number and an expansion of NAPD that is simply not what those letters mean, and a strict copy-only re-read of the same file returned no extractable text at all. Not the applicant, not the county, not that it is an air permit, not that comments are open, not the deadline. This was to have been the deck's closing frame and it is cut.

rejected.finding: Vantage Data Centers TX11 permit O4791 is an AIR permit.
rejected.reason: The agency's hearing page names it only as a permit number and states no program. The word air appears on that page solely as a navigation item. The O prefix is consistent with a federal operating permit and no page reachable this run documents the numbering convention, so the deck says permit and never air permit.

rejected.finding: A stationary gas engine or turbine of this kind requires an air authorization from the environmental agency. This was to be the deck's mechanism claim.
rejected.reason: NOT ESTABLISHED, and the deck's original argument is cut because of it. No agency page reachable this run states the requirement. Seven were checked. The categorical rule sits in Health and Safety Code 382.0518 and 30 TAC 116.110, and both hosts failed to serve text. What survives is weaker and is carried as c14 and c15: engines and turbines sit inside the agency's air permitting programme. The word typically in c14 is load bearing and the agency's own permits by rule pages concede a tier below.

rejected.finding: A bulleted Key Actions and Requirements for Data Center Projects list in the Governor's release.
rejected.reason: An artifact of the fetching tool rather than the page. A first pass rendered bullets the page does not have. A copy only re-read shows seven plain paragraphs. Every quote carried above survived a targeted present or absent pass against the live page.

rejected.finding: That the Odessa power purchase agreement escapes the grid.
rejected.reason: It does not and the deck must not imply it. `immediately adjacent` is a statement about DISTANCE and not about metering, and NOTHING VERIFIED SAYS WHERE THE METER SITS in either direction. The clean behind the meter example is the West Texas one at c16. This reason used to assert that the supplying plant is itself a grid resource, which is the sentence a scorer hard-failed on frame 8, and it survived here for two further rounds.

rejected.finding: That the environmental agency has stopped issuing permits.
rejected.reason: This is a directive rather than a rule and nothing verified says the agency has halted anything. The one enforceable thing in the text is a report back. Every string in this deck says the Governor directed and none says the agency has halted.

rejected.finding: The September 21st release restates that same scope in the same terms.
rejected.reason: Dropped 2026-09-23 in the re-sourcing after the robots violation. The claim was about the September release restating the scope IN THE SAME TERMS, and no permitted host reproduces the release's wording.

rejected.finding: The plant supplying it is an existing gas fired generating facility at Odessa.
rejected.reason: Dropped 2026-09-23 in the re-sourcing after the robots violation. Same host and same reason as c19.

rejected.finding: The company describes that plant as sitting immediately beside the data center site.
rejected.reason: Dropped 2026-09-23 in the re-sourcing after the robots violation. Same host and same reason as c19.

rejected.finding: The water directive ties a missed water survey to permit ineligibility under a named chapter of the Water Code.
rejected.reason: Dropped 2026-09-23 in the re-sourcing after the robots violation. No permitted host carries the Chapter 11 ineligibility language. The Tribune has only a water board official saying entities must respond for certain environmental permits, which is a different speaker and a looser scope.

resourcing: On 2026-09-23 a review found that twelve claims had been fetched from gov.texas.gov with WebFetch, which identifies as ClaudeBot, and that host names ClaudeBot with Disallow: / since 2026-09-17. Nothing was re-fetched from it. Eight were re-sourced verbatim from hosts checked the same day to permit the fetcher (texastribune.org, cbsnews.com, troutman.com), one was split into two for two speakers, and four were dropped. globenewswire.com could not be confirmed and its three claims were dropped with it. Every re-sourced claim is secondary and carries confidence medium, because a law firm or a newspaper reporting a directive is not the directive.
